- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If true outcomes show sharp downward corrections after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the following 5–7 days.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model should not overreact — forecast should lag slightly behind recent highs.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend — apply mean reversion to 3–5 day moving average.  
- For high event count (≥20 events/30d) with net negative supply, forecast should be conservative — avoid upward bias; target 1–2% below recent peak.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and true outcome is rising, model should not overcorrect — allow 1–2% lag in forecast to avoid premature reversal.
